reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600-610/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07), driven in material part by a drop in manual meter-read route completion to 0.88 against a 0.95 target during a field-reader staffing shortfall since July (E-03, E-06), which pushed billing's estimate-substitution step to issue more ESTIMATED-read bills (41% of disputed bills carry read_type ESTIMATED, E-02). This is distinct from the requester's framing: ticket response time is within SLA (E-04) and no tariff change occurred (E-01, E-05), so slow ticket handling and a legitimate rate increase are ruled out as causes.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600-610/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07), driven in material part by billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling='none') misinterpreting raw AMI register values from firmware v4.2 meters (which record in '0.1 m3' vs legacy 'm3', E-13) as anomalous high consumption and rejecting them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), triggering estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-12). This supersedes the requester's slow-response framing (ruled out, within-SLA per E-04) and the earlier field-staffing/route-completion framing (ruled out by E-11), while the mechanism behind the remaining 59% ACTUAL-read disputes stays an open unknown.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
